review.tagline: Design skill that steers coding agents away from generic AI-looking UI
review.summary: Hallmark is a skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that picks a page macrostructure for a brief, applies one of twenty-one themes, and runs fifty-seven slop-test gates plus a self-critique before returning output. It has four verbs: build (default), audit, redesign and study, which extracts design traits from a screenshot or URL. Output is self-contained HTML and CSS.
review.audience: Developers using coding agents who want distinctive front-end design output
strengths: Works across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex from one SKILL.md plus references
Audit verb scores existing code and returns a punch list without editing
Twenty-one themes plus a Custom branch for briefs no theme fits
Live demo site and example pages are linked for each theme
weaknesses: Example output is static HTML and CSS; framework support is not documented
Cursor install needs manual copy into a .mdc rule without frontmatter
No benchmarks showing the slop-test gates improve output
needs: Needs Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, npx
